title: Efectos del aprendizaje adaptativo en el rendimiento académico escolar
abstract: Adaptive learning has gained relevance in school education due to its potential to address classroom heterogeneity and improve academic performance through pathways, content, and feedback tailored to student performance. To this end, the article analyzes the available scientific evidence through an exploratory literature review based on systematic searches in academic databases, explicit selection criteria, and a narrative synthesis of studies focused on school populations. The findings show a generally favorable trend, especially when pedagogical adaptation is combined with teacher mediation, aligned assessment, timely feedback, and solid instructional design; however, the effects vary according to the curricular area, the duration of the intervention, the type of system used, and the implementation conditions. Consequently, it is concluded that adaptive learning can contribute to improving school academic performance, but its effectiveness is not automatic and depends on pedagogical, technological, and contextual decisions that ensure relevance, equity, and educational quality.

title: Design and Implementation of Adaptive Personalized Differential Privacy in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated Learning enables collaborative model training across distributed clients while keeping raw data local, making it attractive for privacy sensitive domains such as healthcare, finance, and edge intelligence. This paper proposes the Design and Implementation of Adaptive Personalized Differential Privacy framework for federated learning that dynamically allocates client specific privacy budgets based on quantified contribution scores. The proposed approach is implemented using PyTorch and Opacus and evaluated on benchmark datasets under non independent and identically distributed data settings. Experimental results demonstrate that the adaptive personalised strategy achieves higher global model accuracy, improved fairness across clients, and a more efficient privacy utility balance compared to uniform differential privacy baselines. Overall, the study confirms that adaptive personalised differential privacy significantly enhances the practicality and robustness of federated learning systems.

title: Submodular Reasoning Pruning: A Diminishing-Returns Training Paradigm for Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) significantly improve performance on complex tasks by generating chain-of-thought (CoT), but they also introduce serious problems of redundant reasoning and computational waste. Existing methods mostly rely on external supervision or heuristic truncation mechanisms, lacking a characterization of the essential structure of reasoning. This paper proposes a novel training paradigm—Submodular Reasoning Pruning (SRP)—which for the first time introduces the principle of diminishing marginal returns from submodular function optimization into reasoning trajectory modeling, formalizing the reasoning process as a problem of maximizing a submodular set function. In this framework, each step of reasoning is treated as a set element, and its contribution is characterized by the submodular function, thus naturally possessing the structural characteristic that "the value of adding more reasoning steps decreases with each step." We further propose a differentiable training mechanism based on greedy approximate optimality, enabling the model to automatically learn the optimal subset of reasoning during the training phase, rather than the complete sequence of reasoning. This method theoretically guarantees the approximate optimality of reasoning compression and mechanistically unifies the processes of "reasoning generation—selection—termination." This paradigm provides an endogenous, structured reasoning control mechanism for LRM, freeing it from dependence on external intervention.

title: Mixed-Integer Reasoning Programming: A Discrete-Continuous Optimization Paradigm for Training Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have significantly improved performance in recent years by generating long reasoning chains. However, their reasoning processes inherently lack structural constraints, leading to problems such as redundant reasoning, uncontrollable computational costs, and uninterpretable reasoning paths. Existing methods (such as Self-Braking and CoT pruning) are mostly based on heuristics or posterior regulation, failing to fundamentally change the reasoning generation mechanism. This paper proposes a novel training paradigm—Mixed-Integer Reasoning Programming (MIRP)—which for the first time introduces the "discrete decision + continuous optimization + global constraints" concept from Mixed Integer Programming (MIP) into the modeling of large model reasoning processes. We formalize the reasoning process as a mixed-integer optimization problem, where each reasoning step corresponds to a discrete decision variable, the reasoning content is represented by continuous variables, and the constraint system encodes logical consistency, minimum reasoning sufficiency, and semantic feasibility. Within this framework, reasoning generation is no longer an unconstrained autoregressive process, but rather transformed into a constrained optimal solution search process. Furthermore, we propose three core mechanisms: (1) Feasible Reasoning Region Learning, (2) Integer Gating of Thought Units, and (3) Dual Reasoning Optimization. This method achieves a unified optimization among reasoning length, logical consistency, and computational cost. This work fundamentally reconstructs the training and reasoning mechanisms of LRM, providing a theoretical foundation for "controllable reasoning" and "optimal reasoning path learning," thus constituting a novel reasoning modeling paradigm.

title: Incentive Mechanism for Federated Learning in Data Heterogeneity and Consumer Privacy Protection
abstract: Consumer privacy protection demands are complex and multifaceted. Traditional incentive mechanisms struggle to balance participation enthusiasm with privacy risk control, leaving consumers exposed to unfair contribution evaluations and privacy leakage risks. To address this, this paper develops a collaborative joint learning incentive mechanism integrating graph neural networks (GNN) and multi-agent reinforcement learning. The approach first constructs node relationship graphs using GNN, then measures data distribution similarity through graph convolutional networks, and finally establishes a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework where nodes act as intelligent agents. By leveraging joint reinforcement learning and a dual-objective reward function, the mechanism optimizes strategies. Experimental results demonstrate that GNN-Shapley achieves over 97% accuracy, while the privacy compensation mechanism elevates average accuracy to 98.27%. This methodology effectively alleviates participation bottlenecks and safeguards consumer rights.

title: Research on the Application of Agent Technology in Special Vehicles
abstract: As modern vehicles evolve toward informatization and intelligentization, special vehicles face challenges such as perception lag, strong decision-making dependence, and information silos, necessitating urgent transformation to adapt to the development of modern vehicles. In this context, agent technology, as a highly autonomous system, can be well integrated with special vehicles. This paper begins by analyzing the operational characteristics of special vehicles and decomposes this complex system into multiple agents with distinct functional features. Secondly, from the perspective of collaborative operation, it constructs multi-agent collaborative operations and, based on this context, establishes typical mission scenarios. Thirdly, it elaborates on the practical application of agents in special vehicles under the framework of information architecture. Finally, it summarizes the developmental advantages of applying agents to special vehicles, aiming to provide references for the intelligent evolution of the special vehicle domain

title: Research on Relation Extraction Methods Based on Heterogeneous Graph Convolutional Neural Networks in Low-Resource Contexts
abstract: In the field of natural language processing, relational extraction techniques are crucial for applications such as knowledge graph construction, information retrieval and intelligent Q&A systems. However, most of the existing relation extraction methods rely on a large amount of annotated data, making it difficult to be implemented in some low-resource languages, while these methods are also affected by the diversity of language expressions, which increases the complexity of extraction. To address the above problems, this paper proposed a relationship extraction method based on heterogeneous graph convolutional neural network (REHGCN), which consists of using the BERT text interpreter for deep understanding of the input text, capturing features in different perspectives through a multi perspective textual feature extraction method, integrating multiple relationships among entities using a heterogeneous graph convolutional neural network, finally deriving the relationship extraction results through a text classifier. The experimental results show that REHGCN can effectively improve the performance of relationship extraction in low resource background, with F1 value of 83.5%, which is significantly better than other existing methods. This research not only provides a novel technical path for relationship extraction in low resource context, but also has significant significance in solving the problems of entity information dispersion.

title: Construction of an English Speech Interaction Teaching System Based on Transformers
abstract: In order to meet the double needs of the user, we have developed a new method of speech interaction, which combines speech modeling, semantic parsing, and multimodal feedback. The system architecture is based on multi-module collaboration, which integrates speech input, Transformer recognition, semantic graph construction, and image feedback. Input features use the log-Mel spectrum supplemented by short-time Fourier transform to extract time-frequency representation. The encoder architecture improves cross-frame modeling by adding a residual fusion strategy to the existing multi-head attention mechanism. In order to improve the performance of context retention, the multistage learning rate scheduling and semantic similarity assistant loss are used in the training. To satisfy the task requirements, a teaching data set with multidimensional annotations, including pronunciation precision, semantic labels, and image feedback, was constructed. Experiments were carried out by comparing the three models. The results show that the precision of the proposed model is 94.28%, the frame level F1 is 0.891, the semantic recall is 89.7%, and the end to end feedback latency is under 410 ms. The feedback interface is stable and adaptable to realize parallel output of voice, image and semantics. The system has proven to be highly scalable and practical in many tasks, such as continuous speech recognition, semantic instruction mapping, and image generation.

title: Attention-Enhanced Multimodal Robotic Arm Lift Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has made significant progress in end-to-end grasping tasks, but existing methods mostly rely on single-modal perception or limited feature modeling, which limits the robustness and generalization ability of the strategies. To this end, this paper proposes an attention enhanced multimodal reinforcement learning framework. Based on the Isaacsim simulation environment and the rsl_rl framework of Isaaclab, it studies the completion of the lift task by the UR5 robotic arm equipped with the Robotiq 85 griper. This framework integrates the robot's body perception state and visual observation into a unified policy network. And embed multiple lightweight attention mechanisms in the visual network to enhance feature representation. A single-object grasping experiment with random initial postures was designed. The Mean reward, Pose position value, and Reward lifting were adopted as core indicators to comparatively analyze the performance of four types of attention mechanisms: channel, spatial, hybrid, and multi-branch. The experimental results show that the attention enhancement model significantly improves the training efficiency and grasping stability of the grasping task. Among them, Global Attention Mechanism (GAM) and Split-Attention Networks (ResNest) performed the best, while Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) could also stably outperform the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) baseline at a lower computational cost. This study comprehensively compared the attention mechanisms in multimodal grasping, confirmed their effectiveness in optimizing reinforcement learning operation strategies, and provided new ideas for visual feature modeling of basic operation tasks of robotic arms.

The experimental results show that the attention enhancement model significantly improves the training efficiency and grasping stability of the grasping task. Among them, Global Attention Mechanism (GAM) and Split-Attention Networks (ResNest) performed the best, while Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) could also stably outperform the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) baseline at a lower computational cost. This study comprehensively compared the attention mechanisms in multimodal grasping, confirmed their effectiveness in optimizing reinforcement learning operation strategies, and provided new ideas for visual feature modeling of basic operation tasks of robotic arms.

title: Dharma, Data and Deception: An LLM-Powered Rhetorical Analysis of Cow-Urine Health Claims on YouTube
abstract: Health misinformation remains one of the most pressing challenges on social media, particularly when cultural traditions intersect with scientific-sounding claims. These dynamics are not only global but also deeply local, manifesting in culturally specific controversies that require careful analysis. Motivated by this, we examine 100 YouTube transcripts that promote or debunk cow urine (gomutra) as a health remedy, focusing on rhetorical strategies such as appeals to authority, efficacy appeals, and conspiracy framing. We employ large language models (LLMs) including GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Mistral Medium 3 to annotate transcripts using a 14-category taxonomy of persuasive tactics. Our analysis reveals that promoters predominantly rely on efficacy appeals and social proof, while debunkers emphasize authority and rebuttal. Human evaluation of a subset of annotations yielded 90.1\% inter-annotator agreement, confirming the reliability of our taxonomy and validation process. This work advances computational methods for misinformation analysis and demonstrates how LLMs can support large-scale studies of cultural discourse online.

title: PanoSAMic: Panoramic Image Segmentation from SAM Feature Encoding and Dual View Fusion
abstract: Existing image foundation models are not optimized for spherical images having been trained primarily on perspective images. PanoSAMic integrates the pre-trained Segment Anything (SAM) encoder to make use of its extensive training and integrate it into a semantic segmentation model for panoramic images using multiple modalities. We modify the SAM encoder to output multi-stage features and introduce a novel spatio-modal fusion module that allows the model to select the relevant modalities and best features from each modality for different areas of the input. Furthermore, our semantic decoder uses spherical attention and dual view fusion to overcome the distortions and edge discontinuity often associated with panoramic images. PanoSAMic achieves state-of-the-art (SotA) results on Stanford2D3DS for RGB, RGB-D, and RGB-D-N modalities and on Matterport3D for RGB and RGB-D modalities. https://github.com/dfki-av/PanoSAMic

title: RouteGuard: Internal-Signal Detection of Skill Poisoning in LLM Agents
abstract: Agent skills introduce a new and more severe form of indirect injection for LLM agents: unlike traditional indirect prompt injection, attackers can hide malicious instructions inside a dense, action-oriented skill that already functions as a legitimate instruction source. We study pre-execution skill-poison detection and show that successful skill poisoning induces a structured internal effect, attention hijacking, in which response-time attention shifts from trusted context to malicious skill spans and drives harmful behavior. Motivated by this mechanism, we propose RouteGuard, a frozen-backbone detector that combines response-conditioned attention and hidden-state alignment through reliability-gated late fusion. Across both real and synthetic open-source skill benchmarks, RouteGuard is consistently the strongest or most robust detector; on the critical Skill-Inject channel slice, it reaches 0.8834 F1 and recovers 90.51% of description attacks missed by lexical screening, showing that defending against skill poisoning requires internal-signal detection rather than text-only filtering

title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Automobile Industry: A Case Study of Tesla’s Dojo Supercomputer
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing entire industries around the world - cars included. Not just a background player, it now shapes how vehicles are built, sold, and driven. Instead of relying on old methods, companies are tapping AI to refine production lines, better support drivers, prevent crashes, and even teach cars to navigate autonomously. One example stands out: Tesla’s Dojo system, custom-made for teaching self-driving software faster. By designing its own brain for learning, Tesla accelerates progress while reducing energy consumption over time. Unusual in design yet effective, this machine demonstrates what algorithms can do when tailored to a single task. Clearly, a shift has happened - machines learn more deeply, react quicker, and drive closer to full independence. All signs point forward; autonomy isn’t waiting, it’s advancing through raw computing power shaped by clear goals.

title: AI-Powered Personal Study Companion: An Intelligent Web Application for Adaptive Learning
abstract: Growing volumes of digital academic content have made effective self-study increasingly difficult for students using conventional tools. This paper presents the AI-Powered Personal Study Companion, a full-stack intelligent web platform that addresses this challenge through four integrated capabilities: automated note synthesis from PDF uploads, multi-level adaptive quiz generation, a real-time academic chatbot, and data-driven performance analytics. The system is built on React.js and FastAPI with a dual-database architecture combining PostgreSQL and MongoDB, secured via JWT authentication. The platform transforms passive reading into an active, personalized learning cycle and aligns with UN SDGs 4, 8, 9, and 10.

title: Matroid-Governed Reasoning: A Structural Independence Paradigm for Training Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Current Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) significantly improve performance by generating long-chain reasoning, but also introduce serious problems of redundant reasoning and structural disorder. Existing methods (such as Self-Braking Tuning) mainly optimize from the perspective of "length control" or "posterior pruning," lacking global constraints on the reasoning structure itself. This paper proposes a novel training paradigm: Matroid-Governed Reasoning (MGR). This method introduces the independence structure from Matroid Theory into the modeling of the reasoning process for the first time, treating the "set of reasoning steps" as a combinatorial structure satisfying the independence axiom, and defining the "optimal reasoning path" as a maximal independent set (basis). Under this framework, reasoning is no longer linearly generated, but a combinatorial selection process constrained by structure. We propose: A Matroid modeling method for reasoning trajectories (Reasoning Matroid) An exchange-based reasoning refinement mechanism (Exchange-based Reasoning Refinement) A Greedy-Optimal Learning Objective (Greedy-Optimal Learning Objective) Basis Consistency Regularization This paradigm fundamentally changes the way LRMs are trained: shifting from "generating more" to "selecting the optimal structure." Theoretically, it is proven that this method can minimize redundancy while ensuring reasoning completeness and naturally avoid overthinking problems.

title: Robust Path Planning via Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for autonomous mobile robot navigation faces several inherent limitations. The stochastic nature of actions generated by DRL policies can undermine performance consistency, while inefficient exploration frequently delays the learning process or prevents the discovery of optimal solutions. This research aims to enhance the robustness of path planning by addressing these challenges. To achieve this goal, we propose a hybrid approach that integrates the flexible decision-making capabilities of deep reinforcement learning with the stability of traditional path planning. The proposed model adopts the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) network as its base. Notably, we pre-process LiDAR point cloud data to extract only essential features for the state representation, thereby preventing performance degradation from high-dimensional inputs and improving computational efficiency. Our model optimizes the learning process through two core strategies. First, it prioritizes experience data generated during training based on negative rewards, guiding the model to learn more frequently from critical failures rather than redundant successes. Second, it dynamically compares the action proposed by the TD3 network with a goal-oriented action from a classical path-planning algorithm in real time. By selecting the action with the higher estimated value, the model guides the policy toward a stable and effective trajectory from the earliest stages of training. To validate the efficacy of our approach, we conducted simulation-based experiments comparing the performance of the proposed model with existing reinforcement learning networks. To ensure statistical significance and mitigate the impact of random initialization, all reported results are averaged over 10 independent runs with different random seeds. The results quantitatively demonstrate that our model achieves significantly higher and more stable reward values, confirming a robust improvement in the path-planning process.

title: Ontological platforms for transdisciplinary STEM education
abstract: The article explores the scientific and technological foundations for the use of ontological platforms and semantic knowledge integration technologies in the context of STEM education development. A comprehensive analysis of modern ontology construction tools that ensure the formalization of knowledge, the establishment of semantic relationships between educational concepts, and the integration of educational resources from different disciplines is conducted. A conceptual model of transdisciplinary STEM ontology is substantiated, which includes the structure of entities, properties, relations, and logical rules and ensures the formation of interdisciplinary connections in the educational process. The architecture of an ontology-driven educational system is proposed, which provides for the integration of semantic knowledge models with analytical modules and cognitive educational services. The possibilities of using ontological platforms to create adaptive educational environments in which automated analysis of educational data, identification of knowledge gaps, and formation of personalized recommendations for students are carried out are considered. The prospects for integrating the developed models into digital educational ECO-systems are revealed, which contributes to the development of intelligent educational services and increases the effectiveness of STEM training.

title: LLM-based data augmentation model for multi-label emotion classification
abstract: Current research in multi-label emotion classification is often constrained by the long-tail distribution of datasets, which impedes the recognition of rare categories and reduces the precision of fine-grained sentiment representation. To address this, we introduce LDAM, a directed data augmentation model that leverages large language models (LLMs) to generate high-fidelity, diverse synthetic samples for data-scarce tail categories. Using RoBERTa as a feature discriminator, the framework extracts nuanced emotional features from the augmented dataset. Experimental results show that LDAM effectively mitigates long-tail imbalances and substantially improves classification performance across complex multi-label scenarios.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Online Course Reviews by Integrating Topic Modeling and Deep Learning——A Topic-Sentiment Matrix Method Based on LDA and BERT
abstract: With the rapid development of massive open online courses, educational platforms have accumulated a vast amount of user comment texts. How to effectively mine learners' sentiment tendencies and focus points from these unstructured data has become a key issue in optimizing course quality. This study proposes an emotion analysis method that integrates topic modeling and deep learning. By combining Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), a topic-emotion fusion matrix is constructed to achieve multi-dimensional fine-grained analysis of online course comments. Firstly, the LDA model is used to mine topics from the comment texts, introducing a Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) weighting mechanism, and the optimal number of topics is automatically determined based on a comprehensive index constructed by topic consistency and perplexity. Secondly, the pre-trained BERT model is utilized for three-class emotion analysis, and a category weight strategy is introduced to alleviate the problem of sample imbalance. Finally, the topic mining results and emotion prediction results are fused to construct a topic-emotion matrix, and the emotional distribution characteristics of each topic are presented through visualization tools such as heat maps and radar charts. Experimental results show that the LDA model identified three core topics: “Teacher Affability and Learning Outcomes”, “Difficulty Level and Learning Outcomes”, and “Homework and Practice and Technical Quality”. The BERT emotion classification achieved an accuracy rate of 98.7% on the test set. The topic-emotion fusion analysis revealed that all topics were mainly positive, but the negative proportion of the “Homework and Practice and Technical Quality” topic was relatively prominent, indicating that there is room for improvement in homework design or the technical platform. This study provides a method reference for the in-depth mining of online course comments and data support for course quality optimization.

title: Research on Optimized Pathways for Constructing Accounting Competency Graphs Based on the BERT Algorithm
abstract: The widespread application of artificial intelligence in financial semantic modeling has driven the deep evolution of methods for constructing financial knowledge graphs. To solve the problems of severe terminology ambiguity, inaccurate relationship extraction, and weak structural updating ability in existing financial and accounting graphs, this paper designs a multi-level graph construction and optimization model that integrates Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) pre trained language model and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). This model implements semantic encoding, entity recognition, relationship extraction, graph fusion, and dynamic updating of financial and accounting texts through a five layer architecture, and introduces a multi-layer semantic embedding mechanism, cluster center loss, and orthogonal constraints to improve representation accuracy. The experiment was based on 23000 financial texts and nearly 40000 pairs of semantic relationships for evaluation. The entity recognition F1-score (F1) score reached 0.872, the relationship extraction Area Under the Curve (AUC) improved to 0.903, and the clustering consistency indicators NMI and Silhouette Score reached 0.83 and 0.68, respectively, which were better than baseline methods such as Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory with Conditional Random Fields (BiLSTM-CRF) and Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach (RoBERTa). Comparative analysis shows that optimizing the path effectively enhances the compactness and expressiveness of the graph structure. The research results indicate that this method has strong universality and scalability in complex financial semantic scenarios, providing technical support for the construction of high-precision financial knowledge graphs and intelligent audit applications.

title: High-Precision and Efficient Robotic Assembly Strategy via Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
abstract: High-precision robotic peg-in-hole assembly under tightened tolerances typically suffers from the curse of dimensionality and extreme sparse rewards, causing severe exploration stagnation in conventional reinforcement learning. To address this challenge without artificially decoupling the continuous assembly process, this paper proposes a progressive Curriculum Reinforcement Learning (CRL) framework based on dynamic tolerance constraints. The framework guides the agent through five progressive stages by smoothly shrinking the target hole size and tolerance threshold down to an extreme 0.8 cm. Furthermore, a Cross-stage Knowledge Preservation Mechanism (C-KPM) is introduced to enable continuous network weight inheritance, effectively eradicating catastrophic forgetting during difficulty leaps. Extensive simulation experiments demonstrate that our CRL-based strategy overwhelmingly outperforms standard baselines in both convergence speed and final success rate. This approach fully preserves end-to-end policy coherence, providing a highly efficient and robust paradigm for flexible manufacturing.

title: Federated Cross-Modal Retrieval with Missing Modalities via Semantic Routing and Adapter Personalization
abstract: Federated cross-modal retrieval faces severe challenges from heterogeneous client data, particularly non-IID semantic distributions and missing modalities. Under such heterogeneity, a single global model is often insufficient to capture both shared cross-modal knowledge and client-specific characteristics. We propose RCSR, a personalization-friendly federated framework that integrates prototype anchoring, retrieval-centric semantic routing, and optional client-specific adapters. Built on a frozen CLIP backbone, RCSR leverages lightweight shared adapters for global knowledge transfer while supporting efficient local personalization. Prototype anchoring helps unimodal clients align with global cross-modal semantics, and a server-side semantic router adaptively assigns aggregation weights based on retrieval consistency to mitigate alignment drift during heterogeneous updates. Extensive experiments on MS-COCO, Flickr30K, and other benchmarks show that RCSR consistently improves global retrieval accuracy and training stability, while further enhancing client-level retrieval performance, especially for clients with incomplete modalities. Code is available at https://github.com/RezinChow/RCSR-Retrieval-Centric-Semantic-Routing.

title: SMP: Reusable Score-Matching Motion Priors for Physics-Based Character Control
abstract: Data-driven motion priors that can guide agents toward producing naturalistic behaviors play a pivotal role in creating life-like virtual characters. Adversarial imitation learning has been a highly effective method for learning motion priors from reference motion data. However, adversarial priors, with few exceptions, need to be retrained for each new controller, thereby limiting their reusability and necessitating the retention of the reference motion data when applied to downstream tasks. In this work, we present Score-Matching Motion Priors (SMP), which leverages pre-trained motion diffusion models and score distillation sampling (SDS) to create reusable task-agnostic motion priors. SMPs can be pre-trained on a motion dataset, independent of any control policy or task. Once trained, SMPs can be kept frozen and reused as general-purpose reward functions to train new policies to produce naturalistic behaviors for downstream tasks. We show that a general motion prior trained on large-scale datasets can be repurposed into a variety of style-specific priors. Furthermore, SMP can compose different styles to synthesize new styles not present in the original dataset. Our method can create reusable and modular motion priors that produce high-quality motions comparable to state-of-the-art adversarial imitation learning methods. In our experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of SMP across a diverse suite of control tasks with physically simulated humanoid characters. Video available at https://youtu.be/jBA2tWk6vzU

title: Contrastive Semantic Projection: Faithful Neuron Labeling with Contrastive Examples
abstract: Neuron labeling assigns textual descriptions to internal units of deep networks. Existing approaches typically rely on highly activating examples, often yielding broad or misleading labels by focusing on dominant but incidental visual factors. Prior work such as FALCON introduced contrastive examples -- inputs that are semantically similar to activating examples but elicit low activations -- to sharpen explanations, but it primarily addresses subspace-level interpretability rather than scalable neuron-level labeling. We revisit contrastive explanations for neuron-level labeling in two stages: (1) candidate label generation with vision language models (VLMs) and (2) label assignment with CLIP-like encoders. First, we show that providing contrastive image sets to VLMs yields candidate labels that are more specific and more faithful. Second, we introduce Contrastive Semantic Projection (CSP), an extension of SemanticLens that incorporates contrastive examples directly into its CLIP-based scoring and selection pipeline. Across extensive experiments and a case study on melanoma detection, contrastive labeling improves both faithfulness and semantic granularity over state-of-the-art baselines. Our results demonstrate that contrastive examples are a simple yet powerful and currently underutilized component of neuron labeling and analysis pipelines.

title: GCImOpt: Learning efficient goal-conditioned policies by imitating optimal trajectories
abstract: Imitation learning is a well-established approach for machine-learning-based control. However, its applicability depends on having access to demonstrations, which are often expensive to collect and/or suboptimal for solving the task. In this work, we present GCImOpt, an approach to learn efficient goal-conditioned policies by training on datasets generated by trajectory optimization. Our approach for dataset generation is computationally efficient, can generate thousands of optimal trajectories in minutes on a laptop computer, and produces high-quality demonstrations. Further, by means of a data augmentation scheme that treats intermediate states as goals, we are able to increase the training dataset size by an order of magnitude. Using our generated datasets, we train goal-conditioned neural network policies that can control the system towards arbitrary goals. To demonstrate the generality of our approach, we generate datasets and then train policies for various control tasks, namely cart-pole stabilization, planar and three-dimensional quadcopter stabilization, and point reaching using a 6-DoF robot arm. We show that our trained policies can achieve high success rates and near-optimal control profiles, all while being small (less than 80,000 neural network parameters) and fast enough (up to more than 6,000 times faster than a trajectory optimization solver) that they could be deployed onboard resource-constrained controllers. We provide videos, code, datasets and pre-trained policies under a free software license; see our project website https://jongoiko.github.io/gcimopt/.

title: AgentSearchBench: A Benchmark for AI Agent Search in the Wild
abstract: The rapid growth of AI agent ecosystems is transforming how complex tasks are delegated and executed, creating a new challenge of identifying suitable agents for a given task. Unlike traditional tools, agent capabilities are often compositional and execution-dependent, making them difficult to assess from textual descriptions alone. However, existing research and benchmarks typically assume well-specified functionalities, controlled candidate pools, or only executable task queries, leaving realistic agent search scenarios insufficiently studied. We introduce AgentSearchBench, a large-scale benchmark for agent search in the wild, built from nearly 10,000 real-world agents across multiple providers. The benchmark formalizes agent search as retrieval and reranking problems under both executable task queries and high-level task descriptions, and evaluates relevance using execution-grounded performance signals. Experiments reveal a consistent gap between semantic similarity and actual agent performance, exposing the limitations of description-based retrieval and reranking methods. We further show that lightweight behavioral signals, including execution-aware probing, can substantially improve ranking quality, highlighting the importance of incorporating execution signals into agent discovery. Our code is available at https://github.com/Bingo-W/AgentSearchBench.

title: A Graph Neural Network Framework for Structural Side-Channel Vulnerability Assessment in Cryptographic Circuits
abstract: Traditional side-channel analysis treats power and electromagnetic traces as temporal sequences, applying statistical or sequence-based machine learning methods without regard for the circuit topology responsible for generating observed leakage. This discards structural information intrinsic to digital circuits: gate connectivity, signal propagation topology, and the hierarchical organization of cryptographic modules. A framework is presented that applies Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to side-channel vulnerability assessment by modeling circuits as attributed graphs in which nodes represent logic gates, edges represent wire connections, and power measurements are encoded as node features. A complete pipeline is developed spanning Verilog netlist parsing, graph construction, and Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) training with multi-head attention for multi-scale circuit analysis. Evaluation on ten AES-128 circuit implementations demonstrates an 86.4% attack success rate, compared with 68.1% for a CNN-LSTM baseline, with required power traces reduced from 988 to 790. Cross-architecture generalization reaches 63.5% accuracy on unseen circuit families, substantially above the 18.7% random baseline. Interpretable vulnerability heatmaps localize leakage sources at the gate level, enabling pre-silicon security assessment before fabrication.

title: SAE Information Theory I: The 4DD Ontology of Information and a Single Foundational Axiom / SAE 信息论 I:信息的 4DD 本体论与一条基础公理
abstract: Full bilingual text and framework available at self-as-an-end.net Abstract (English) Shannon information theory provides a complete theoretical apparatus at the operational level. Within its defined scope, H=−∑plog⁡pH = -\sum p \log p H=−∑plogp as a statistical functional on probability distributions precisely quantifies uncertainty and encodability at the source/readout layer. For nearly eight decades Shannon's framework has grounded the foundational language of communication, coding, and computation. This paper does not treat Shannon information theory as an adversary; rather, building on E=Ic3E = Ic^3 E=Ic3 from the Mass Series convergence paper, it relocates Shannon information theory as the complete theory of the 1DD operational projection layer, while providing information with its 4DD ontological status. This paper adopts one foundational axiom: energy-information is conserved across the 4DD total space (across all 42 1DDs and across all DD channels). Combined with 4DD closure asymmetry—4DD as closure level, whose operational category is encapsulation, admits no reverse operation internally—and the framework-level observation that non-equilibrium dynamics in the 4DD open sphere provide net transfer into the I channel, four structural consequences unfold: the arrow of time, causality, propagation, and reception. These are structural entailments of the axiom combined with the 4DD closure structure, not mutually independent axioms. This paper positions itself as a foundational paper, constructing the ontological ground only and leaving full formalism for subsequent papers. Alongside the foundation, this paper provides three concrete interface readings: a conditional ontological reading of ln⁡2\ln 2 ln2 in Landauer's principle as the projection factor between continuous measurement formalism and discrete substrate; the Bekenstein bound as a specific algebraic instance of the HH H-II I relation at saturation condition; and the black hole information paradox reframed through 42-channel scope expansion. These three share a coherent reading pattern in the SAE framework—a shared ontological motif of Planck-tick discrete substrate with continuous measurement layer—but are not claimed to be formally derived from a common mechanism; the three carry different commitment loads and are independently evaluable. The general mathematical relation between Shannon's H and SAE's I, the complete information-side formalism of 42-channel conservation, the spacetime formal development of propagation, and the structural constraints on reception endpoints—all remain open tasks for future papers in the information theory series. The series builds on the Mass Series convergence paper (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19510869) which established E = Ic³ as the 4DD physical substrate of information. The paper takes a continuation posture: it does not replace or revise Shannon information theory, but relocates Shannon as the complete theory of the 1DD operational projection layer, while providing the 4DD ontological ground that Shannon's scope does not engage. Alongside the ontological foundation, the paper provides three concrete interface readings (§4.5) engaging existing problems in the information theory community: (a) Conditional ontological reading of ln 2 in Landauer's principle as the projection factor between continuous measurement formalism and discrete substrate; (b) Bekenstein bound reinterpreted as a specific algebraic instance of the H-I relation at saturation condition via E = Ic³ substitution; (c) Black hole information paradox reframed through 42-channel scope expansion, compatible with the Page curve as a single-channel mathematical structure while providing different ontological ground. These three interface readings share a coherent ontological motif (Planck-tick discrete substrate plus continuous measurement layer) but are not claimed to be formally derived from a common mechanism. They carry different commitment loads (Low / Medium / High) and are independently evaluable—not a package deal. The consciousness-level reading (13DD continuous simulator on discrete substrate) is listed as an optional deeper interpretation, not as prerequisite for the core arguments. Claim-status map (§6.1) is provided to enable readers to immediately trace the epistemic status of each claim—inherited structural result, foundational postulate, structural consequence, interface reading, or open task. This transparency is the paper's basic methodological commitment. Subsequent papers in the series will unfold the open problems listed in §7, including: (1) general mathematical relation between Shannon's H and SAE's I (partial anchor: saturation instance in §4.5.2); (2) complete information-side formalism of 42-channel conservation (qualitative reframing: §4.5.3); (3) spacetime formal development of propagation; (4) structural constraints on reception endpoints (bridging to biological, consciousness, and AI information); (5) formal derivation of Landauer's principle as internal consequence of E = Ic³ (conditional reading: §4.5.1). title: Vero: A Coherence-Guaranteed Language for Neural Architecture Specification
abstract: Vero is a declarative language for specifying neural network architectures with compile-time coherence guarantees. Unlike existing configuration formats such as JSON or YAML, a Vero program cannot be compiled if it violates structural coherence. Every declaration carries four base properties — truth, harmony, time, and place — verified statically before lowering to an intermediate representation. Dissonant declarations produce compile errors, not warnings. This paper describes the language design, type system, coherence rules, and the current Vero Lite compiler implementation in Rust.

title: CampusMentor - Student Career and Placement Guidance System
abstract: Campus placement preparation is a crucial determinant of students’ career outcomes, yet many institutions rely on inefficient, fragmented, and non-adaptive evaluation processes. This study presents CampusMentor, an AI-driven student analytics and career guidance system designed to enhance placement preparation through structured, data-driven methodologies. The system evaluates student performance across coding, aptitude, and technical domains, identifies strengths and learning gaps, and provides personalized improvement strategies and career recommendations. By integrating continuous performance tracking with intelligent analytics, CampusMentor improves transparency, consistency, and decision-making in placement workflows. Experimental observations indicate improved accuracy in skill assessment, better career clarity for students, and reduced manual effort for mentors. The proposed approach demonstrates the effectiveness of combining analytics and AI-driven recommendations to optimize student readiness and institutional placement efficiency.

title: A Chinese Grammatical Error Correction Method Based on Knowledge Distillation and Retrieval Enhancement
abstract: Chinese grammatical error correction (CGEC) is a pivotal task in natural language processing, with significant implications for enhancing the quality of language instruction and text editing. While current large language model (LLM)-based approaches exhibit strong performance, they often struggle with low-frequency or syntactically complex errors. Conversely, conventional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques frequently fail to incorporate grammatical knowledge with sufficient precision. To address these limitations, we propose SA-RAGEC, a novel CGEC framework that integrates knowledge distillation with syntax-aware retrieval augmentation. First, we leverage a large language model to distill a structured knowledge base from parallel corpora via knowledge distillation, explicitly encoding error types, root causes, and correction rationales. Subsequently, we design a syntax-aware encoder based on contrastive learning to construct a vector space capable of disentangling semantic and syntactic representations, thereby enabling precise retrieval of syntactically isomorphic error instances. Finally, we employ a multi-stage "diagnose–retrieve–rerank" pipeline to select high-quality exemplars, which are then used in a chain-of-thought prompting strategy to guide the LLM in analogical reasoning and error correction. Experimental results on benchmark datasets—including FCGEC and MuCGEC—demonstrate that SA-RAGEC, built upon the Qwen3-8B-Base foundation model, achieves an F0.5 score of 50.76, substantially outperforming both baseline methods and the original LLM. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of both the syntax-aware retrieval mechanism and the chain-of-thought guidance. This work presents a practical and effective approach to equipping large models with precise grammatical knowledge, thereby advancing the state of the art in Chinese grammatical error correction.

title: Using Prompt-based AI to Identify Chinese Mirative Constructions
abstract: This study investigates the use of prompt-based artificial intelligence (AI) to identify mirative constructions in Mandarin Chinese using the large language model (LLM) GPT-3.5-turbo. Mirativity, a semantic category expressing surprise or unexpectedness, is expressed through both non-parasitic and parasitic mirative constructions in many languages, including Mandarin. The study compares the effectiveness of zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies on a corpus of 200 Mandarin sentences. Results show that few-shot prompting improved performance, increasing recall from 39% (zero-shot) to 55%, with overall accuracy rising from 66% to 76%. Despite these improvements, challenges remain in accurately identifying mirative markers and parasitic constructions. The findings highlight the potential of prompt-based AI in linguistic research, though limitations in recall and labelling precision suggest the need for further refinement. This approach offers a time- and resource-efficient tool for linguists, but human validation remains crucial for robust analysis.

title: Design and Optimization of a Dual-Loop Fuzzy Control System for an Inverted Pendulum Based on an Adaptive Genetic Algorithm
abstract: The inverted pendulum represents a classic benchmark system characterized by pronounced nonlinearity, strong coupling, and inherent instability. Conventional fuzzy control approaches encounter two primary obstacles: the curse of dimensionality, which leads to an exponential explosion in the rule base, and the heavy reliance on expert knowledge for defining membership function parameters. This paper proposes a dual-loop fuzzy control strategy augmented by an adaptive genetic algorithm to address these challenges. Initially, a parallel and series dual-loop architecture is employed to decouple the four-dimensional state space, thereby partitioning the complex control task into separate angle and position regulation loops. This decomposition effectively compresses the size of the fuzzy rule repository. Subsequently, a novel two-tier nested composite gene encoding scheme is devised. The first tier combines heterogeneous genes representing membership function parameters, rule consequents, and output scaling factors within a single fuzzy inference engine. The second tier concatenates these composite genomes across multiple fuzzy engines. This structure enables simultaneous and autonomous optimization of all controller parameters, eliminating subjective manual calibration. At the implementation level, the physical model of the inverted pendulum is exported as a C++ class using MATLAB/Simulink code generation tools, thereby establishing a high-fidelity simulation environment. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with a conventional Linear Quadratic Regulator, the genetically optimized parallel dual-loop fuzzy controller achieves comprehensively superior performance compared with LQR, fuzzy PID, and sliding-mode–LQR composite control strategies, exhibiting markedly improved dynamic response and robustness. This research enriches the design methodology that integrates adaptive fuzzy control with evolutionary optimization, and it offers a new engineering pathway for the robust stabilization of strongly nonlinear systems.

title: Engineering robust quantum resources from maximal violations of subcorrelation Bell inequalities
abstract: Abstract Bell inequalities have long been essential for the device-independent detection of entanglement. This study introduces subcorrelation Bell inequalities as a robust framework for detecting entanglement and probing quantum non-locality. We derived a family of such inequalities, categorized according to their dependence on measurement settings, and numerically identified 19 distinct quantum states that achieve the maximal violation of these inequalities. Importantly, our focus on maximal violation is not for its own sake but because, in this framework, maximal violation directly corresponds to maximal robustness of nonlocal correlations against particle loss. This connection reveals a broad class of multipartite entangled states that remain resilient under loss, making them highly relevant for practical implementations of quantum information protocols. We further characterized their entanglement properties using concurrence and the geometric measure, confirming their utility for critical areas such as quantum communication, cryptography, and device-independent protocols. The framework established herein sets the stage for future investigations, including the generalization of these inequalities to higher-dimensional systems and a more comprehensive characterization of their robustness against various forms of noise, thereby expanding the potential for non-local states to drive progress in quantum technologies.

title: RL Token: Bootstrapping Online RL with Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models can learn to perform diverse manipulation skills "out of the box," but achieving the precision and speed that real-world tasks demand requires further fine-tuning -- for example, via reinforcement learning (RL). We introduce a lightweight method that enables sample-efficient online RL fine-tuning of pretrained VLAs using just a few hours of real-world practice. We (1) adapt the VLA to expose an "RL token," a compact readout representation that preserves task-relevant pretrained knowledge while serving as an efficient interface for online RL, and (2) train a small actor-critic head on this RL token to refine the actions, while anchoring the learned policy to the VLA. Online RL with the RL token (RLT) makes it possible to fine-tune even large VLAs with RL quickly and efficiently. Across four real-robot tasks (screw installation, zip tie fastening, charger insertion, and Ethernet insertion), RLT improves the speed on the hardest part of the task by up to 3x and raises success rates significantly within minutes to a few hours of practice. It can even surpass the speed of human teleoperation on some of the tasks.

title: OntoLogX: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Extraction from Cybersecurity Logs with Large Language Models
abstract: System logs represent a valuable source of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), capturing attacker behaviors, exploited vulnerabilities, and traces of malicious activity. Yet their utility is often limited by lack of structure, semantic inconsistency, and fragmentation across devices and sessions. Extracting actionable CTI from logs therefore requires approaches that can reconcile noisy, heterogeneous data into coherent and interoperable representations. We introduce OntoLogX, an autonomous Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to transform raw logs into ontology-grounded Knowledge Graphs (KGs). OntoLogX integrates a lightweight log ontology with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and iterative correction steps, ensuring that generated KGs are syntactically and semantically valid. Beyond event-level analysis, the system aggregates KGs into sessions and employs a LLM to predict MITRE ATT&CK tactics, linking low-level log evidence to higher-level adversarial objectives. We evaluate OntoLogX on both logs from a public benchmark and a real-world honeypot dataset, demonstrating robust KG generation across multiple KGs backends and accurate mapping of adversarial activity to ATT&CK tactics. Results highlight the benefits of retrieval and correction for precision and recall, the effectiveness of code-oriented models in structured log analysis, and the value of ontology-grounded representations for actionable CTI extraction.

title: KT4EQG: Personalized Exercise Question Generation via Knowledge Tracing
abstract: Educational Question Generation (EQG) aims to synthesize customized exercise questions that enhance student learning. An effective EQG system should ideally personalize questions for each student by modeling the student's knowledge state and generating questions that provide the greatest learning benefit. However, few existing EQG approaches are able to achieve such fine-grained personalization. In this paper, we explore how EQG can benefit from knowledge tracing (KT), which models students' knowledge states based on historical performance and predicts future performance. We propose KT4EQG, a personalized EQG framework that generates effective questions for individual students under the guidance of a KT model. Specifically, KT4EQG seeks to maximize a student's potential improvement in overall knowledge mastery by leveraging the KT model to select the most suitable knowledge concept for the student to practice. An LLM-based question generator is then trained to produce a question faithfully grounded in the selected concept. Experimental results on XES3G5M and MOOCRadar show that KT4EQG consistently generates more effective questions than methods with limited or no personalization.

title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Shared Syntactic Mechanisms in Language Models
abstract: While language models demonstrate sophisticated syntactic capabilities, the extent to which their internal mechanisms align with cross-constructional principles studied in linguistics remains poorly understood. This study investigates whether models employ shared neural mechanisms across different syntactic constructions by applying causal interpretability methods at a granular level. Focusing on filler-gap dependencies and negative polarity item (NPI) licensing, we utilize activation patching to identify the functional roles of specific attention heads and MLP blocks. Our results reveal a highly localized and shared mechanism for filler-gap dependencies located in the early to middle layers, whereas NPI processing exhibits no such unified mechanism. Furthermore, we find that these mechanisms identified by activation patching generalize to out-of-distribution, while distributed alignment search, a supervised interpretability method, is susceptible to overfitting on narrow linguistic distributions. Finally, we validate our findings by demonstrating that the manipulation of the identified components improves model performance on acceptability judgment benchmarks.

title: Fundamentação Teórica da Arquitetura Hierárquica de Coerência Quântica (AHCQ): Estabilização do Estado Fundamental e Resolução da Discrepância Energética do Vácuo"
abstract: ABSTRACTA presente publicação formaliza a *Arquitetura Hierárquica de Coerência Quântica (AHCQ)*, um framework teórico e técnico disruptivo projetado para a implementação de sistemas de computação quântica com supressão exponencial de erro e estabilização intrínseca de fase. O modelo propõe uma mudança de paradigma ao tratar a decoerência não como uma perda inevitável, mas como um elemento passível de engenharia espectral e topológica através da manipulação do ambiente e do vácuo.A fundamentação lógica e matemática desta arquitetura é uma evolução direta dos mecanismos de processamento não-linear estabelecidos pela autora no trabalho *"Binário Fractal" (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19730873)*, utilizando a geometria fractal para a estruturação de dados em múltiplas escalas de conectividade estável.Ademais, a viabilidade física e a rigidez do sistema AHCQ são sustentadas pela resolução analítica apresentada na obra *"Resolução da Densidade de Energia do Vácuo (ρv)" (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19740224)*. Nesta arquitetura, a discrepância energética do vácuo — tradicionalmente vista como um obstáculo na física teórica — é convertida em um parâmetro ativo de blindagem. Através de uma hierarquia espectral definida por \gamma_k = \gamma_0 r^k e uma filtragem de ruído de baixa frequência (1/f) de ordem N, o sistema garante que a coerência não seja apenas preservada, mas construída dinamicamente pela própria topologia da rede.Este registro consolida a integração entre a física fundamental de partículas, a mecânica quântica e a engenharia de hardware assistiva, constituindo um ativo intelectual proprietário fundamental para o desenvolvimento da tecnologia Silva-Tech e o avanço rumo à computação quântica tolerante a falhas em escala real.*Sugestão de Palavras-chave (Keywords) para preencher no Zenodo:*Quantum Computing, AHCQ, Silva-Tech, Vacuum Energy, Fractal Binary, Quantum Error Correction, 1/f Noise Filtering, Theoretical PhysICS.

title: Secure Machine Learning Architectures for Edge-Based IoT Systems: Threat Models, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: The application of machine learning (ML) at a high rate in edge-based Internet of Things (IoT) systems has improved real-time decision-making in cyber-physical systems (CPS). Nevertheless, adversarial manipulation, data poisoning, and lifecycle vulnerability are threats to the dependability and security of these distributed architectures. The review summarizes the existing studies on adversarial threats and secure architectural solutions to edge-based IoT ML systems and focuses on time-series models, distributed learning environments, and model lifecycle security. An organized literature review is done under adversarial machine learning, federated learning security, IoT vulnerability analysis, AI supply chain protection, and governance frameworks. The mitigation strategies, threat models, and attack mechanisms were evaluated in the context of edge and CPS deployment. It has been found that inference-time evasion, training-time poisoning, federated aggregation manipulation, and lifecycle vulnerabilities all increase the attack surface of distributed IoT systems. Time-series models have the characteristic vulnerability to cumulative perturbation and drift exploitation. Multi-layered defenses such as strong training, secure aggregation, data provenance checking, ongoing monitoring, and alignment of governance are important to mitigate. The need to achieve edge-based IoT ML system security requires combined architectural, technical, and governance strategies that mitigate adversarial risks throughout the entire model lifecycle and maintain the real operational reliability of the model.

evidence.title: Secure Machine Learning Architectures for Edge-Based IoT Systems: Threat Models, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigation Strategies
evidence.abstract: The application of machine learning (ML) at a high rate in edge-based Internet of Things (IoT) systems has improved real-time decision-making in cyber-physical systems (CPS). Nevertheless, adversarial manipulation, data poisoning, and lifecycle vulnerability are threats to the dependability and security of these distributed architectures. The review summarizes the existing studies on adversarial threats and secure architectural solutions to edge-based IoT ML systems and focuses on time-series models, distributed learning environments, and model lifecycle security. An organized literature review is done under adversarial machine learning, federated learning security, IoT vulnerability analysis, AI supply chain protection, and governance frameworks. The mitigation strategies, threat models, and attack mechanisms were evaluated in the context of edge and CPS deployment. It has been found that inference-time evasion, training-time poisoning, federated aggregation manipulation, and lifecycle vulnerabilities all increase the attack surface of distributed IoT systems. Time-series models have the characteristic vulnerability to cumulative perturbation and drift exploitation. Multi-layered defenses such as strong training, secure aggregation, data provenance checking, ongoing monitoring, and alignment of governance are important to mitigate. The need to achieve edge-based IoT ML system security requires combined architectural, technical, and governance strategies that mitigate adversarial risks throughout the entire model lifecycle and maintain the real operational reliability of the model.

title: ES-SAC: A hybrid evolution strategy and reinforcement learning approach for humanoid locomotion control
abstract: State-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning (DRL) techniques such as Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) demonstrate promising results in developing control strategies. In this study, we propose ES-SAC, a hybrid learning framework that integrates Evolutionary Strategy (ES) with the SAC algorithm to enhance humanoid robot locomotion control. ES-SAC leverages the global search capabilities of evolutionary algorithms and the sample efficiency and convergence properties of DRL. The performance of the ES-SAC agent was evaluated on a bipedal robot simulation and compared to other hybrid methods employing deterministic agents, including ES-TD3 and ES-DDPG. The ES-SAC agent exhibited superior average reward performance and a more stable learning process. In contrast, the ES-TD3 agent achieved faster course completion but exhibited control instabilities. This study also highlights the importance of physical and behavioral metrics – such as torque efficiency, horizontal and vertical deflection, and Q0 values – in assessing the reliability of DRL-based locomotion control. Our findings suggest that relying solely on cumulative reward for evaluation can be misleading, underscoring the need for a more comprehensive analysis in future research.

title: Research on Multi-Agent Collaborative Fine-Grained Sentiment Classification for Ukrainian-English Translated Texts
abstract: Sentiment analysis, as a core task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), plays a critical role in cross-lingual public opinion monitoring. Fine-grained sentiment classification with approximately ten categories for Ukrainian is of great significance for accurately understanding the diverse public opinion tendencies of relevant issues worldwide. However, when processing translated texts, existing methods often suffer from semantic shift, ambiguity, and knowledge obsolescence, leading to sentiment. Single models lack self-verification during the reasoning process, resulting in limited robustness in complex multi-sentiment scenarios. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes a multi-agent collaborative cross-lingual sentiment classification framework, which mainly consists of two core agents: the QA agent is responsible for preliminary sentiment reasoning and label prediction on translated texts, and the RAG agent enhances context-aware sentiment judgment by retrieving similar annotated samples from an external knowledge base. Experimental results show that on the Qwen-turbo model, after introducing the RAG mechanism, the classification accuracy increases from 0.0789 to 0.2268. On the Deepseek-chat-chat model, the accuracy rises from 0.0851 to 0.2708. These significant improvements verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in enhancing the accuracy and robustness of cross-lingual sentiment classification, providing a new feasible approach for low-resource language sentiment analysis.

title: Mechanism of Generative AI Interaction Experience on Consumer Trust and Consumption Behavior
abstract: Generative AI has transformed digital commerce from static recommendation to iterative, language-based co-decision making. Yet existing studies remain fragmented: computer-science research often emphasizes model alignment and generation quality, whereas consumer research usually isolates trust, attitude, or purchase intention without explaining how these outcomes emerge from the underlying computational pipeline. To address ACM's emphasis on computer-technology-centered research, this paper develops a computationally grounded mechanism framework that explicitly highlights recent progress in computer technology, including foundation-model capability, RLHF-aligned dialogue optimization, retrieval-augmented generation, memory-aware personalization, explainable response construction, uncertainty estimation, and trust-state monitoring. We formalize how observable system signals—semantic relevance, personalization fit, explanation transparency, controllability, privacy exposure, and response inconsistency—are translated into consumer evaluations of competence, warmth, and risk, and we model trust as a dynamic state variable that updates across repeated interactions. An illustrative simulation shows that advances in retrieval grounding, transparent reasoning, editable memory, privacy-preserving control, contradiction detection, and intervention logging can jointly improve robustness, inspectability, and deployability of conversational commerce systems. The resulting framework contributes not only to consumer-behavior theory but also to the improvement of computer technology for trustworthy generative-AI applications by providing a modular architecture, measurable system metrics, and engineering guidance for optimizing recommendation acceptance, user trust, and purchase conversion.

title: A Governance Mechanism Construction Path for Social Data under the Context of Hengqin–Macao Integration
abstract: Artificial intelligence and intelligent algorithms provide computable technical pathways for cross-border social data governance. To enhance the timeliness, accuracy, and compliance of social data governance within the Qianhai-Macau integration context, this paper constructs a computational model for governance challenges. Employing multimodal feature modelling, integrated text-image feature learning, and collaborative computation under privacy constraints, it conducts joint analysis and optimisation of cross-domain social data. The method's efficacy is validated through system implementation and simulation evaluation. Results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces privacy risks while elevating risk identification rates to over 86%, effectively mitigating tail latency and markedly enhancing governance stability. The study concludes that this approach achieves a balance between performance and compliance under governance constraints, providing verifiable technical support for constructing social data governance mechanisms within the Qianhai-Macau integration context.

title: rFedKD-LSR: reverse federated knowledge distillation with low-rank server reconstruction
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) faces significant challenges in communication efficiency and Non-IID data adaptation, largely due to global model redundancy and inefficient downlink transmission. To address these issues, we propose rFedKD-LSR, a reverse federated knowledge distillation framework based on server-side low-rank reconstruction. This method utilizes a one-off Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and feature self-distillation to generate lightweight models for deployment. Furthermore, a reverse knowledge distillation strategy aggregates client-side soft predictions to effectively mitigate parameter drift caused by data heterogeneity. System experiments on MNIST, FashionMNIST, SVHN, and EMNIST demonstrate that rFedKD-LSR reduces communication rounds by 40%–80% while maintaining superior performance. Notably, in highly heterogeneous scenarios (α = 0.05), the proposed method achieves 94.30% accuracy on MNIST, significantly outperforming advanced baselines (82.33%), providing an efficient solution for resource-constrained edge environments.

title: Comparative Benchmarking of TD3 for Multi-Stage Indoor Navigation
abstract: For autonomous systems operating in environments lacking Global Positioning System (GPS) signals, indoor Mapless navigation via Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a promising end-to-end solution. However, existing work often overlooks the unique demands of “multi-stage indoor navigation. While ordinary indoor navigation typically focuses on point-to-point movement within consistent environment types, multi-stage navigation requires an agent to adapt to a sequence of tasks characterized by abrupt topological shifts-such as transitioning from expansive hallways into dense, cluttered rooms. The core challenge in this multi-stage setting is the policy instability caused by environmental distribution shifts, which frequently leads to catastrophic mode collapse or severe performance degradation in traditional DRL algorithms. To address this, we evaluate the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) framework against the traditional Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) baseline and the State-of-the-Art (SOTA) Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. Utilizing an escalating training setup-progressing from empty spaces to complex multi-obstacle rooms-we analyze how TD3's Clipped Double Q-learning and delayed policy updates mitigate value estimation bias under shifting constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that TD3 achieves a stable average reward of 0.62 in the final stages, whereas DDPG and PPO plateau near 0.5. Quantitative analysis indicates that TD3 yields a 22 % higher mission success rate and significantly faster recovery during environment transitions compared to the baselines. These findings prove that structural constraints in value estimation are essential for managing distribution shifts in multi-stage navigation. Ultimately, this work provides a scalable and resilient framework for high-fidelity autonomous systems, offering critical technical support for the deployment of industrial robots in unpredictable and GPS-denied operating conditions.

title: How Hard Is Continuous Clustering? Lower Bounds from the Existential Theory of the Reals
abstract: This paper studies the computational difficulty of clustering problems that are defined directly on a continuous probability density. Rather than working with finite samples, we assume the density is given as a polynomial and ask whether it contains certain cluster structures. Four natural questions are examined. First, do there exist several points with high density that are far apart from each other. Second, do two high density points have a midpoint with low density, creating a valley between them. Third, does the region where the density is above a threshold have at least a given number of separate connected pieces. Fourth, does that same region contain a hole, meaning a loop that cannot be shrunk to a point. We prove that the first two problems, separated points and valley detection, are exactly as hard as the existential theory of the reals, a complexity class that contains NP and is believed to be strictly larger. In contrast, the topological problems of counting connected pieces and detecting holes are at least as hard as the existential theory of the reals, but their exact complexity remains open. Placing them inside that class would need a major advance in real algebraic geometry. These results give the first rigorous classification of exact continuous clustering inside the real polynomial hierarchy. They also show that even basic clustering criteria are not NP complete unless unexpected collapses occur.

title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Truly Understand Small Objects?
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown promising potential in diverse understanding tasks, e.g., image and video analysis, math and physics olympiads. However, they remain blank and unexplored for Small Object Understanding (SOU) tasks. To fill this gap, we introduce SOUBench, the first and comprehensive benchmark for exploring the small objects understanding capability of existing MLLMs. Specifically, we first design an effective and automatic visual question-answer generation strategy, constructing a new SOU-VQA evaluation dataset, with 18,204 VQA pairs, six relevant sub-tasks, and three dominant scenarios (i.e., Driving, Aerial, and Underwater). Then, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation on 15 state-of-the-art MLLMs and reveal their weak capabilities in small object understanding. Furthermore, we develop SOU-Train, a multimodal training dataset with 11,226 VQA pairs, to improve the SOU capabilities of MLLMs. Through supervising fine-tuning of the latest MLLM, we demonstrate that SOU-Train can effectively enhance the latest MLLM's ability to understand small objects. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that, the proposed SOUBench, along with the SOU-VQA and SOU-Train datasets, provides a crucial empirical foundation to the community for further developing models with enhanced small object understanding capabilities. Datasets and Code: https://github.com/Hanfj-X/SOU.

title: Quantum simulation of massive Thirring and Gross-Neveu models for arbitrary number of flavors
abstract: The study of fermionic quantum field theories is an important problem for realizing the standard model of particle physics on a quantum computer. As a step towards this goal, we consider the massive Thirring and Gross--Neveu models with arbitrary number of fermion flavors, $N_f$, discretized on a spatial one-dimensional lattice of size $L$ in the Hamiltonian formulation. We compute the gate complexity using the higher-order product formula and using block-encoding/qubitization and quantum singular value transformations in the limit of large $N_f$ and $L$. We also prepare the ground states of both models with excellent fidelity for system sizes up to 20 qubits with $N_f = 1,2,3,4$ using the adaptive-variational quantum imaginary time algorithm. In addition, we also classify the dynamical Lie algebras of these relativistic fermionic models and show that they belong to the same isomorphism class. Our work is a concrete step towards the quantum simulation of real-time dynamics of large $N_f$ fermionic quantum field theories models relevant for chiral symmetry breaking, understanding dimensional transmutation, and exploring the conformal window of field theories on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
